results.reader_what: A grant-topic map portrays science as more applied and mission-oriented than conventional citation-based maps.
results.reader_why: Grant portfolios can reveal funding priorities and organisational positions that publication maps may understate.
results.reader_more: The authors model roughly 81,000 EU grants from 2003–2024 using text embeddings, clustering and topic labelling, then build a global science map and overlays for regions, universities and funders. The approach is useful for portfolio analysis because grants encode planned research and policy missions. Topic boundaries still depend on modelling choices and grant-text quality.

deep_analysis.research_question: Can EU grant texts support a useful global map of science for portfolio and science-policy analysis?
deep_analysis.main_finding: The resulting map is more applied and mission-oriented than citation-based science maps and supports portfolio overlays.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: EU grant corpus, SPECTER embeddings, clustering and BERTopic-style keyword labelling, with stability-guided topic selection and portfolio overlays.
deep_analysis.qualification: Topic models simplify multidimensional research activity and depend on textual/algorithmic choices.
deep_analysis.radar_relevance: Directly uses the EU research-funding portfolio to create a science-policy mapping tool.
